nodes.label: Design goals
nodes.rationale: Goals include private start flow, tracked group buttons, per-group settings, silent removal, owner-only controls, native user-picker whitelisting, complete content-type coverage, no-rights DMs, and persistent storage.

nodes.label: Plan architecture
nodes.rationale: Architecture uses no FSM and no webhooks, only long polling.

nodes.label: Global implementation constraints
nodes.rationale: Constraints include aiogram v3 patterns, required env, default-allow, non-deleted service messages, English UI, and exhaustive callback prefixes.

nodes.label: format_stats helper
nodes.rationale: format_stats emits removed messages with non-zero type counts or nothing removed yet.

nodes.label: Per-group removal counters
nodes.rationale: Counters are maintained per content type per group and displayed only to the owner as removed messages.

nodes.label: is_command_exempt(message)
nodes.rationale: Command exemption detects text starting with / and a bot_command entity at offset zero.

nodes.label: Command exemption when text blocked
nodes.rationale: When text is blocked, messages starting with / whose bot_command entity is at offset zero are exempt so other bots continue working.

nodes.label: BotFather group privacy off
nodes.rationale: Group Privacy must be disabled in BotFather or the bot never sees normal group messages.

nodes.label: Group privacy requirement
nodes.rationale: BotFather Group Privacy must be OFF or the group handler never sees normal messages.

nodes.label: aiogram 3.31.0 pinned
nodes.rationale: The project pins aiogram 3.31.0 and uses its v3 router, filters, and keyboard patterns.

nodes.label: Implementation stack constraints
nodes.rationale: Stack is Python with aiogram 3.31.0, PostgreSQL, and long polling, with group privacy OFF.

nodes.label: Implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Plan implements the design as a single async polling process with pure classify, asyncpg DB layer, three routers, and keyboard builders.

nodes.label: Telegram Media Remover Bot design
nodes.rationale: The bot sits above Telegram permissions and silently deletes blocked content types regardless of whether the sender is a regular member or an admin; only whitelisted users bypass the blocks. Success is zero group noise plus private owner-only per-group counters.

nodes.label: bot.py entrypoint
nodes.rationale: Entrypoint creates bot and dispatcher, initializes DB and schema, includes routers, and starts polling with message, edited_message, my_chat_member, and callback_query updates.

nodes.label: Callback data protocol
nodes.rationale: Exact callback prefixes include group, types, toggle, white, unwhite, stats, reset_stats, reset_group, back_groups, and noop.

nodes.label: classify(message)
nodes.rationale: classify returns the first present field in priority order or None for service and unknown messages.

nodes.label: classify module
nodes.rationale: classify is pure, duck-typed against aiogram Message fields, and centralizes content-type detection.

nodes.label: CONTENT_TYPES priority list
nodes.rationale: CONTENT_TYPES orders story_forward, photo, video, video_note, voice, audio, document, animation, sticker, poll, contact, location, venue, dice, game, invoice, successful_payment, checklist, then text.

nodes.label: reset_group_data helper
nodes.rationale: reset_group_data wipes blocked, whitelist, and stats while retaining the groups row.

nodes.label: should_delete helper
nodes.rationale: Pure should_delete returns False for None, self, command-exempt, whitelisted, or unblocked types; anonymous senders fall through to type checks.

nodes.label: handlers_group router
nodes.rationale: Group router deletes blocked non-whitelisted messages for groups and supergroups, handles edited messages, and throttles no-rights DMs.

nodes.label: keyboards module
nodes.rationale: Keyboard builders create inline group menus, type toggles, whitelist lists, and the native request_users picker.

nodes.label: handlers_private router
nodes.rationale: Private router handles /start, group lists, owner-gated menus, type toggles, stats, and reset commands.

nodes.label: Review focus
nodes.rationale: Review checks anonymous channel photo deletion, captioned photo classification, command exemption, edited message recheck, and non-owner denial.

nodes.label: texts constants
nodes.rationale: texts module provides START, GROUPS_EMPTY, GROUP_TITLE, NEED_ADMIN, NOT_OWNER, CONNECTED, and STATS_EMPTY constants.

nodes.label: Integration test marker
nodes.rationale: Integration tests need a live database and run only with POSTGRES_DSN_TEST.

nodes.label: RemoveUnnes Telegram Media Remover Bot
nodes.rationale: README presents the bot as silently deleting blocked message types in groups, even from admins, with whitelist bypass and private owner-only stats.

nodes.label: pytest dependency
nodes.rationale: Development dependencies include pytest for unit and integration tests.

nodes.label: Blocked content types list
nodes.rationale: Coverage includes text, photo, video, video_note, voice, audio, document, animation, sticker, poll, contact, location, venue, dice, game, invoice, successful_payment, story_forward, and checklist.

nodes.label: Content-type coverage
nodes.rationale: All real Telegram message content types are individually blockable, based on aiogram Message media fields.

nodes.label: Group message handling flow
nodes.rationale: Group messages are classified, checked against whitelist and blocked types, deleted and counted when blocked, with edited messages rechecked.

nodes.label: Admin delete rights requirement
nodes.rationale: The bot must be added to a group as admin with Delete Messages rights or deletion is impossible.

nodes.label: Delete rights requirement
nodes.rationale: The bot needs group admin rights with can_delete_messages; otherwise it skips deletion and DMs the owner.

nodes.label: Anonymous and channel-post handling
nodes.rationale: Messages without from_user cannot match the whitelist and are judged by content type only; bot self messages are always skipped.

nodes.label: Design anti-goals
nodes.rationale: The bot must not post anything into the group on deletion, leak one group's data to another or to non-owners, delete service messages or its own admin notices, or cap the whitelist.

nodes.label: Caption does not reclassify media
nodes.rationale: classify priority places text last, so a captioned photo or video is classified as media rather than text.

nodes.label: Above Telegram permissions
nodes.rationale: Normal group restrictions cannot help because some senders are admins; restricting them would require demotion, which owners avoid, so the bot deletes above Telegram permission levels.

nodes.label: Design non-goals
nodes.rationale: Non-goals exclude warnings, mutes, bans, global lists, keyword filters, group-visible logs, multi-owner roles, and webhook deployment.

nodes.label: Owner-only control and stats
nodes.rationale: Only the user who started and added the bot for a group can change its settings or view its stats.

nodes.label: Service messages never deleted
nodes.rationale: Service messages such as new_chat_members, left_chat_member, pinned_message, chat_shared, and users_shared are never deleted and classify returns None.

nodes.label: Silent removal
nodes.rationale: Deletions produce no group-visible message, notice, warning, or log; owner sees stats privately on demand.

nodes.label: graphify knowledge graph
nodes.rationale: Project AGENTS.md records that graphify-out contains the knowledge graph and directs agents to query it before browsing raw source files.

nodes.label: Bot setup workflow
nodes.rationale: Setup requires creating the bot, disabling Group Privacy, starting Postgres, configuring env, and adding the bot as group admin with Delete Messages.

nodes.label: pytest-asyncio dependency
nodes.rationale: Development dependencies include pytest-asyncio for async test execution.

nodes.label: docker-compose PostgreSQL db service
nodes.rationale: Local Postgres 15 service uses removable username, password, database, port, and a pgdata volume.

nodes.label: pgdata volume
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL data persists in the named pgdata volume across container restarts.

nodes.label: config.Settings and load
nodes.rationale: config loads BOT_TOKEN and POSTGRES_DSN and raises RuntimeError when either is missing.

nodes.label: init_pool(dsn)
nodes.rationale: init_pool creates an asyncpg connection pool from the configured DSN.

nodes.label: init_schema(pool)
nodes.rationale: Schema uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and includes owners, groups, blocked, whitelist, stats, pending_greetings, and notify_state.

nodes.label: db module
nodes.rationale: The DB module manages asyncpg pool, schema creation, queries, and pure moderation helpers.

nodes.label: register_group and ownership transfer
nodes.rationale: register_group returns created, kept, or fresh_start and implements same-owner keep versus different-owner wipe.

nodes.label: flush_pending helper
nodes.rationale: flush_pending sends deferred connected-group notices during /start.

nodes.label: handlers_membership router
nodes.rationale: Membership router tracks bot additions/removals, ownership transfer, fresh starts, and pending greetings.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL DSN configuration
nodes.rationale: Runtime requires POSTGRES_DSN pointing at the remover PostgreSQL database.

nodes.label: asyncpg dependency
nodes.rationale: Async PostgreSQL access is provided directly by asyncpg.

nodes.label: blocked table
nodes.rationale: blocked stores the selected blocked content types per chat; absence means allowed.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL schema tables
nodes.rationale: Schema includes owners, groups, blocked, whitelist, stats, and optional pending_greetings or notify_state metadata.

nodes.label: groups table
nodes.rationale: groups stores chat IDs, owner association, title, and added timestamp.

nodes.label: notify_state table
nodes.rationale: notify_state stores last notification timestamps for throttling no-rights DMs.

nodes.label: owners table
nodes.rationale: owners stores owner user IDs and creation timestamps.

nodes.label: pending_greetings table
nodes.rationale: Pending greetings store deferred connected-group notices for owners who have not started the bot yet.

nodes.label: stats table
nodes.rationale: stats stores removal counts per content type per chat.

nodes.label: whitelist table
nodes.rationale: whitelist stores per-chat user IDs with optional username and display and added timestamp.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL persistence
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL stores settings and counters so restart preserves configuration.

nodes.label: No-rights DM throttle
nodes.rationale: When deletion fails due to insufficient rights, the owner is DM'd at most once per group per ten-minute window.

nodes.label: Re-add by different owner transfers ownership with fresh start
nodes.norm_label: re-add by different owner transfers ownership with fresh start
nodes.rationale: If the bot is re-added by a different user, blocked, whitelist, and stats rows are wiped, owner_id transfers, and defaults are restored.

nodes.label: Pending greetings for undmessaged owners
nodes.rationale: Telegram forbids DMing users who never started the bot, so a pending greetings row is stored and flushed on first /start.

nodes.label: Per-group isolation
nodes.rationale: Blocked types, whitelist, and counters are isolated per group and default allow everything.

nodes.label: Re-add by same owner keeps settings
nodes.norm_label: re-add by same owner keeps settings
nodes.rationale: Re-adding the bot by the same owner preserves existing group settings, counters, and whitelist.
